outputs.claim-account.md:
# Claim account: Quote checking

No write brief was supplied, so the commission is the only statement of intent.
It does not contradict itself. The note is an explanatory topic treatment of
quote checking in general. It covers what each kind of check establishes, which
assumptions make a result meaningful, and what stays unverified. It is not a
procedure and not a description of Commonplace commands. It does not need to
defend one overarching claim. ADR 046, ADR 073 and ADR 094 (S1–S3) are one
system's design records. They may be used as bounded cases, abstracted-from
origins, or illustrations. None of them is universal authority, and none
corroborates the general claims (collection contract, "Origin is not
corroboration"). The derived-copy note (S4) is a theory note. The note applies
it only as far as its preconditions reach (see §12).

Claim mode: unless a section says otherwise, the general claims below are
universal conceptual claims about what a check's inputs can license. A reader
refutes one by giving a re-derivable case: a check of the named kind that
licenses the denied inference. Mark inferences and reasoning beyond the sources
as such in the prose. Put open points in `## Open Questions` and limits in
`## Scope` (type contract).

Ordering is advisory. Lead with §1 and §2, the core distinction between a label
and a check, and what a match is relative to. Follow with the inferences a match
does and does not license (§3–§6), then the evidence a check read (§7–§10), then
the derived-copy framing (§12). Section headings are the writer's choice, and
the commission does not require an outline.

## 1. A label asserts fidelity; only a check that could fail it makes the label informative

- **Treatment:** state it. This is the supported core of the commission's "a
  label alone cannot establish fidelity" point. Do not reuse the incumbent's
  wording or taxonomy.
- **Basis:** A1 (the `verbatim` marker was "hand-maintained and trusted" before
  checking), A3 (only `verbatim` can be mechanically falsified, while the other
  markers "never claimed exact text"), I5, H2, inference N7.
- **Scope and qualifiers:** a check has three outcomes: confirmed, refuted, and
  unresolved. An unresolved result neither confirms nor refutes the label (H2).
  A label whose claim has no mechanical test, such as a paraphrase or a
  provenance label, stays an authored assertion. Give the reason: such a label
  makes no claim about exact text, and no derivation rule exists for it (A3, I3).
  Do not cite A3's reference to the incumbent note as support. It is
  compatibility information only.
- **Dependencies:** none. Most of the note builds on this section.
- **Destination:** opening, as the mechanism the note explains.

## 2. Wording agreement is decidable only relative to a quoted span, an identified source text and a normalization rule

- **Treatment:** state it as the note's main mechanism, and mark the
  over-normalization direction as inference.
- **Basis:** A2 (strict substring test against the linked source), C1
  (normalization is "load-bearing", and under-normalization gives false
  mismatches, "worse than no check"), C3, C4 (S3 establishes occurrence "under
  its normalization rule"), C5, G1–G2, inference N1.
- **Scope and qualifiers:** "matches" means "matches under rule R against bytes
  B". If any of the three inputs changes, the verdict can change. Under-
  normalization produces false failures (sourced). Over-normalization passes
  differences a reader could care about, such as case, emphasis and punctuation.
  That direction is inference (gap G-f). Support it with B1's mismatch
  categories, framed as the kinds of difference involved, not as prevalence.
  C2's choice of normalization by source kind may illustrate that the rule can
  be fixed per source kind and not per citation. It is one design's choice, not
  a requirement.
- **Dependencies:** §1.
- **Destination:** early body, right after §1.

## 3. Whether choosing a normalization rule is itself mechanical is unsettled

- **Treatment:** leave it as an open question and give both sides. Do not
  resolve it.
- **Basis:** conflict K2. S1 calls the test "strict substring" while calling
  normalization load-bearing, and S3 selects normalization by source kind. S4's
  fourth precondition says a derivation rule that is a judgment call is "the
  forbidden state, just relocated one layer down" (I3). Inference N8 also leaves
  this open.
- **Scope and qualifiers:** once a rule is fixed, applying it is mechanical.
  Choosing the rule may embed a judgment about which differences matter. The
  sources do not settle whether that choice weakens the mechanical status of the
  check.
- **Dependencies:** §2, §12.
- **Destination:** `## Open Questions`, with a sentence in the body near §2 or
  §12.

## 4. Finding the words in a source is weaker than locating the cited passage

- **Treatment:** state it. Present uniqueness and containment as ways to narrow
  the match, not as required policy.
- **Basis:** D1 ("Presence and range bounds alone do not establish that the cited
  passage occupies the location an author gives it"), D2, D3 (disjoint extracts
  cannot be concatenated into a synthetic passage), D4 (guidance alone cannot
  enforce containment), inference N2.
- **Scope and qualifiers:** S3's "exactly one occurrence, or exactly one inside a
  given range" is one policy that makes occurrence identity mechanical. A policy
  that accepts any occurrence licenses a weaker inference: the words appear
  somewhere, not "this passage". Present the trade-off, not the policy. The
  point about concatenation can stand as a general hazard: separately matched
  pieces can pass while the passage they imply never exists.
- **Dependencies:** §2.
- **Destination:** body, after §2, as the second thing a check can establish.

## 5. A passing match licenses no inference about context, support, relevance or truth

- **Treatment:** state it firmly. It transfers beyond S3 because string
  comparison carries no semantic test (Scope note in the reconstruction).
- **Basis:** E1 ("Finding one occurrence cannot establish that its context
  supports the attached claim"), E2 ("does not establish truth, relevance, or
  semantic support"), E3 (unchanged words with changed interpretive context go
  undetected), E4 (storing exact copies of claims would still not establish
  support), inference N3.
- **Scope and qualifiers:** support and contextual interpretation are semantic
  judgments. Truth of the quoted claim is a further step that the sources do not
  treat as checkable (gap G-d). The note may say truth is outside every check
  discussed here. It must not describe how truth would be assessed.
- **Dependencies:** §2, §4.
- **Destination:** body, central. This is the main limit the note explains.

## 6. Wording agreement, attribution, contextual interpretation and truth are distinct questions

- **Treatment:** the commission requires this distinction. State it as a
  conceptual distinction built by explicit reasoning. Present only wording
  agreement and contextual support as treated by the sources. Mark attribution
  and truth as questions the discussed checks do not reach.
- **Basis:** wording agreement: §2, §4. Contextual interpretation and support:
  E1–E5. Truth: E2 only (G-d). Attribution: no support (G-b). The sources treat
  source identification (H1, G1–G2), not whether quoted words are correctly
  ascribed to a speaker inside the source.
- **Scope and qualifiers:** define each term in the note, because the sources
  leave "fidelity", "attribution" and "contextual interpretation" undefined
  (G-h). For attribution, give the reasoning and label it as reasoning: a
  source can itself quote someone else, so the words can match the source
  exactly while being misattributed to the source's author. Do not cite support
  for this. Keep "source identification", meaning which document the check
  read, separate from "attribution", meaning who said the words.
- **Dependencies:** §2, §5, §11.
- **Destination:** early. It frames the other sections and can sit with §1 or
  just after it.

## 7. A result's meaning depends on which evidence the check actually read

- **Treatment:** state it. The commission requires three separate states:
  material the system retains, material currently accessible to this checker,
  and material this check used.
- **Basis:** F1 (a fresh checkout keeps identity and checksum, "not the complete
  captured source"), F3, F4 (a quotes-only route "never silently falls back to a
  local snapshot"), F5 (falling back to whatever is available makes a pass or a
  fail depend on "ambient cache state"), F6 ("does not imply that the separate
  snapshot check ran on this machine"; missing bytes "never count as verified"),
  G2, inference N4.
- **Scope and qualifiers:** the general point does not depend on Commonplace's
  untracked-snapshot storage (reconstruction Scope). Use S2 and S3 as a bounded
  case of a design that keeps these states apart. Missing source bytes are a
  different outcome from a mismatch. They leave the label unverified, not false.
  Do not merge any of these states with "current model context" (see §8).
- **Dependencies:** §1, §2, §11.
- **Destination:** body, start of the evidence half of the note.

## 8. A bounded selection of a source can keep each passage exact while losing the context some judgments need; context budget is one cause of selection

- **Treatment:** state the retained-evidence point with a qualifier. State the
  context-budget point as the commission's premise plus reasoning, with no cited
  support. Keep it subordinate to the note's purpose and do not make it an
  organizing argument.
- **Basis:** F3 (a bounded verbatim passage "may contain enough"; some claims
  depend on "broad, distributed, or contextual material"), F7 (minimum passages
  for a later check), A1, inference N5. The context budget appears in no source
  (G-e).
- **Scope and qualifiers:** if a source is larger than the available model
  context, the context holds a selective or compressed representation. That
  implies neither lossy storage in the wider system nor inexactness of any
  selected passage (commission, Must keep). Selection limits which judgments are
  possible, especially contextual and support judgments. It does not limit the
  exactness of what was selected. Model context, retained evidence and the
  evidence a check used are three different things and must not be conflated
  (commission, Must exclude).
- **Dependencies:** §5, §7.
- **Destination:** body, inside or right after §7, kept short.

## 9. Checking against an interpretation of a source adds a semantic hop

- **Treatment:** state it for paraphrase and analysis. Its extension to quote
  chains is inference (§10).
- **Basis:** F2 (checking a note against a paraphrase "creates two semantic hops,
  and rewording at either hop can change the proposition"), F1 (summaries "are
  interpretations. They are not source text"), inference N6.
- **Scope and qualifiers:** each hop is a separate place where the proposition
  can shift. A check is direct only when its input is source text.
- **Dependencies:** §5, §7.
- **Destination:** body, evidence half.

## 10. With an intermediary source, exactness against the intermediary and fidelity to the original are separate checks

- **Treatment:** state it as inference, and flag it as reasoning that no
  supplied source makes.
- **Basis:** gap G-a. J1 (the `second-hand` marker exists and is unchecked) is
  the only mention. Inference N6 is an analogy. Conflict K1: S1 presents the
  markers as alternatives, but the commission forbids treating second-hand
  provenance and verbatim wording as mutually exclusive, and the commission
  governs.
- **Scope and qualifiers:** a quotation can be verbatim against the intermediary
  that the checker holds while it remains unverified against the original. Each
  link in the chain needs its own check against the text at that link, with
  that link's identity and normalization (§2, §11). Provenance and wording are
  separate properties of one citation. Do not offer a chain-checking design.
  Upstream authenticity, meaning whether the captured source faithfully
  represents its origin, is unverified by any check discussed (G-c). Name it as
  a remainder, not as a solved or solvable step.
- **Dependencies:** §2, §7, §9, §11.
- **Destination:** body, evidence half, followed by a `## Scope` or
  `## Open Questions` entry.

## 11. Source identity and version determine which text a verdict is about

- **Treatment:** state it with a qualifier. Present the version-binding
  trade-off as inference.
- **Basis:** G1 (changed bytes are a new observation), G2 ("Equal bytes do not
  bind a local path to the ingest being cited"), G3 (current-byte checks catch a
  removed passage but not unrelated appends; hash-pinning "cannot distinguish
  relevant changes from unrelated appends"), E3, G4, inference N9.
- **Scope and qualifiers:** a checksum establishes byte identity, not which
  source a citation means. Pairing a citation with a source is a separate step.
  Checking against current bytes is stable under unrelated edits, but it misses
  interpretive context that changed while the quoted words stayed the same.
  Pinning detects every edit but does not separate relevant edits from
  irrelevant ones. Neither approach shows that the context the author read is
  the context present now. Avoid Commonplace terms such as "ingest" and
  `snapshot_sha256` as general stages. If the note uses them, scope them to the
  case (commission, Must exclude).
- **Dependencies:** §2, §7.
- **Destination:** body, evidence half.

## 12. The rule for checking derived copies covers wording agreement, but not quote checking as a whole

- **Treatment:** state it as inference. Assess S4's applicability and do not
  import S4's strongest claims.
- **Basis:** I1–I3 (checked-or-absent; the asymmetry between an absent copy and
  a false copy; four preconditions, with natural-language judgments excluded),
  I4 (judgment-based dependents need managed staleness and review), I6 (S1
  claims all preconditions hold for `verbatim`), inference N8.
- **Scope and qualifiers:** for wording agreement, the preconditions plausibly
  hold: a fixed rule, a locatable span with a named source, and source bytes
  present. That explains why exact-wording checks are worth having, and why an
  unchecked label risks silent error and not just an absent assurance. The
  preconditions fail for context and support, which have no derivation rule.
  They also fail at validation time when source bytes are absent (F1, F6). The
  normalization question (§3) bears on the fourth precondition. Link S4 as a
  theory note that the argument extends or applies. It is not corroboration.
- **Dependencies:** §1, §2, §3, §5, §7.
- **Destination:** body, late. This section explains why some checks are
  mechanical and others are not.

## 13. Contextual support needs a separate judgment against adequate evidence

- **Treatment:** state it with a qualifier, as the consequence of §5 and §12.
  Do not describe a gate or command.
- **Basis:** E5 (a separate semantic check reads retained quotes or the full
  pinned source), F3, F4 (if retained quotes are insufficient, the check fails
  and does not fall back), I4.
- **Scope and qualifiers:** this judgment is not mechanical, and its result
  depends on the evidence it read (§7). Mention Commonplace's semantic gate at
  most as a scoped example. The commission excludes documenting current
  commands.
- **Dependencies:** §5, §7, §12.
- **Destination:** body, near §12.

## 14. Every result is conditioned on extraction assumptions: which spans count as assertions and which source each span is paired with

- **Treatment:** state it with a qualifier, briefly.
- **Basis:** H1 (the source is the adjacent link, paired by proximity), H2
  (extraction is incomplete, and "unresolved" reports that openly), H3
  (demonstrations "show" rather than "assert"; scanning them gives false
  mismatches), H4 (ground truth lies outside the document), inference N10.
- **Scope and qualifiers:** proximity pairing and fence neutralization are one
  design's heuristics. The general point is that a checker must decide what is a
  quotation claim and what it cites. Errors in that decision produce false
  mismatches or silent omissions before any matching runs.
- **Dependencies:** §1, §2.
- **Destination:** body or `## Scope`, short.

## 15. Observed mismatch kinds in one prototype

- **Treatment:** state it with a qualifier, as an illustrative case.
- **Basis:** B1. Of 87 candidates, 63 matched, 18 mismatched and 6 were
  unresolved, with no false mismatch on manual audit. Mismatches were dominated
  by editorial omission, bracketed substitution, case changes and punctuation
  moved inside the quotation.
- **Scope and qualifiers:** one prototype, one sibling corpus, one
  normalization, one historical measurement. It shows which kinds of
  divergence occurred there, not how common they are. Do not use it as
  corroboration of a general claim. Optional: the writer may use only the
  mismatch categories, or leave the case out.
- **Dependencies:** §2.
- **Destination:** optional illustration inside §2.

## 16. Whether marked editorial alterations should count as verbatim

- **Treatment:** leave it as an open question.
- **Basis:** gap G-g. Ellipses and bracketed insertions appear only as causes of
  mismatch (B1).
- **Scope and qualifiers:** the note may say that accepting marked alterations
  would change what a match certifies, which bears on §2's normalization point.
  It must not propose a convention.
- **Dependencies:** §2, §15.
- **Destination:** `## Open Questions`.

## 17. Severity policy, referential-check cost and historical syntax

- **Treatment:** leave it out, or at most use it as a scoped example.
- **Basis:** A4 (fail, warn and pass severities), H4's cost framing, C2 and D2
  policy details, and K3 (S2's list-item form and unverified locators were
  amended by S3, and S3 was partly amended by ADR 105).
- **Scope and qualifiers:** these are Commonplace selections. If the note
  mentions S2's "authored locators rather than mechanically verified anchors"
  (D5), treat it as a historical case of the presence-versus-location gap, not
  as current state. A locator note that carries context but is not evidence
  (D5, S3) may illustrate §4.
- **Dependencies:** none.
- **Destination:** omit, or use as a brief scoped example.

## 18. Decisions reserved for the operator

- **Title and path:** the user authorized the topic title "Quote checking" and
  the collection-convention exception. The workflow keeps the incumbent title,
  H1 and path for this candidate. Do not shape the body to defend that heading.
  Report that the retitle remains for the session agent after publication
  approval.
- **Type and traits:** keep `types/note.md` and remove `title-as-claim`. Choose
  other traits by content. `has-external-sources` does not apply, because no
  external sources are commissioned.

# Writing conventions for kb/theory/

## Text contract and explanatory-reach

This collection retains **beliefs about the design space** — truth-apt claims
that explain how systems of this kind can work, including bounded claims about
one fixed design. A claim may be grounded in or bounded to a particular system,
including Commonplace, when it preserves the particular's proposition-relative
scope and contributes more than the selected value or resulting state.
Truth-aptness of a local observation alone does not place it here.

Apply the placement test to the artifact's intended contribution: **after every
named system choice is recoverably scoped, does a substantive claim about the
design space remain?** A fixed choice needs stable reidentification at every
distinction that could change truth or licensed inference. A ranged choice
needs a recoverable range and valuation rule. A substantive witness needs the
universal prohibition it contradicts or the existence claim it verifies. If scoping leaves only what Commonplace
selected or the current or historical state that selection produced, the
artifact belongs in `kb/reference/`.

The claim that remains after scoping is a new universal hypothesis, not a
summary of the particulars it came from: no number of singular observations
establishes a universal statement ([Popper, *Logic of Scientific Discovery*,
§§13–15](../sources/popper-logic-of-scientific-discovery.ingest.md)). Link the
cases it was generalized from as `abstracted-from`; they explain its origin
and do not corroborate it. A particular system may still appear as the case a
universal claim is applied to: the claim supplies the law, and the system's
selections supply the initial conditions (§12).

Quality goal is **explanatory-reach** — the most general formulation the argument supports, with boundaries mapped. A note with explanatory-reach compresses many situations into one explanation.

Tests for explanatory-reach:
- Change one premise — can you predict the change in the conclusion?
- Would the insight apply in a different domain?
- Could someone say exactly how it's wrong, not just that it's incomplete?
- Does it account for where the pattern actually works and fails, not just why it should?

Notes that only record "X works" are adaptive — useful but brittle. Explaining *why* X works gives explanatory-reach. Explanatory-reach is a direction, not a gate.

Apply explanatory-reach to claim formulation:
- State the claim under the weakest assumptions the argument actually uses.
- Treat qualifiers in the title, description, opening claim, and main proof as obligations. If a qualifier does not change the reasoning when removed, drop it from the claim or move it to an application, corollary, or scope note.
- Keep real boundaries explicit. A boundary belongs in the claim when the argument depends on it; otherwise it belongs in `## Scope`, `## Caveats`, or a nearby narrower application note.
- Prefer a general lemma plus narrower consequences over a narrow lemma whose extra assumptions are only needed by one downstream use.

**Don't defend against objections you've already closed.** A clause that pre-empts a misreading the previous clause already ruled out doesn't add rigor, it pads: "a hypothesis to be tested, not a definitional truth" — being a hypothesis to be tested already means it isn't one. State the claim once; let review catch what still needs defending.

**Admit real gaps instead of hedging around them.** Precision means an agent can't misread the claim — it does not mean stacking qualifications against every conceivable pushback. When the argument has an actual gap — an assumption you can't yet defend, a case you haven't worked through — name it plainly in `## Scope` or `## Open Questions` as an opening for later investigation. A named gap is more useful than one padded shut with defensive language, and it's what review and later notes are for.

**Formulation constraint — scope the choices you name.** For every named system
choice, the title, description, and opening argument must preserve the
proposition-relative reference rule or range and the role that choice plays.
Those can come from the surface itself or from context the intended consumer is
guaranteed to receive. A fixed opaque design may use stable reidentification
when hidden identity distinctions cannot change truth or licensed inference. A
ranged variable needs a recoverable range and valuation rule. A substantive
witness must state which universal prohibition the instance contradicts or
which existence claim it verifies; a single instance cannot support a
universal claim (§15). Literal quantifier
syntax is neither necessary nor sufficient. Substitution can expose dependence
on a local term, but the consumption boundary decides whether its scope is
missing. If no substantive claim remains after each choice is scoped, move the
artifact to `kb/reference/` because its intended contribution is what
Commonplace selected or the state that selection produced. Claims later in the
body obey the same scoping rule; explicitly scoped local reports and examples
may serve as the theory's origin, illustration, or test without becoming the
artifact's intended contribution; only a test counts as corroboration (see
"Origin is not corroboration").

**Theory-independence constraint.** The claim must stand if any single cited description is removed — otherwise it's still a description.

**Design-shaped artifacts need a theoretical claim.** A construction may stay here when it witnesses a substantive truth-apt existential claim. Mark its [residual selections as choices](./artifact-classification-separates-content-kind-lineage-and-authority.md), not as evidence that the selections are uniquely correct. The requirements must be substantive enough that exhibiting any witness is informative; otherwise the unadopted design belongs in `kb/reference/proposals/` under [ADR 028](../reference/adr/028-design-proposals-live-in-reference-proposals.md). Proposal status is a workflow state, not an information kind.

**Hypotheses stay recognizable in prose.** State the conjectural force in the title, description, opening, or a clearly named hypotheses/open-questions section. `user-verified: true` may attest that a note responsibly presents a conjecture; it does not turn the conjecture into established fact.

**Claim modality (ADR 066, ADR 091).** A claim asserts in one of three modes, and the mode determines what refutes it. **Universal** — the default reading for any claim that does not state otherwise. A counterexample refutes it when others can check it again: a specified case whose conflict with the claim any reader can re-derive, or an observed effect shown to recur. A single unrepeated report of an exception raises a problem to test; it does not by itself refute ([Popper, *Logic of Scientific Discovery*, §22](../sources/popper-logic-of-scientific-discovery.ingest.md)). A contradiction refutes the claim together with the conditions it was applied under (§18), so a refutation names which part it blames: the claim, or those conditions. **Statistical** — the claim states a tendency ("usually", "most", "under conditions C"); a single instance does not refute it, prevalence evidence does — and the claim must still forbid something: state the comparison, conditions, or rate that prevalence evidence could refute, or the tendency is vacuous. This stated-refuter requirement is Popper's treatment of probabilistic claims (§§65–68) made per-claim: a frequency claim is strictly unfalsifiable until a refuting prevalence is fixed in advance, and here that decision lives in the claim text rather than in a field-wide convention. **Ideal-type** — the claim states a deliberately simple first-order model whose exceptions are conceded and accounted for; what refutes it is an exception the domain treats as ordinary unmarked practice, or the model losing explanatory dominance — see [domain pricing routes an exception to idealization assessment but does not decide it](./domain-pricing-routes-an-exception-to-idealization-assessment.md). Ideal-type acceptance and refutation are comparative — inference to the best explanation with its virtues (declared use, mechanism, bound, dominance) written as attackable commitments rather than reviewer judgment; the bound is absolute, so "best available" alone never suffices. A priced exception is Lakatos's anomaly rather than a refuter: it earns the claim an idealization assessment, and the adequacy record then decides the verdict. Declare the mode in the claim text itself — title, thesis, or a named section; an ideal-type claim carries its adequacy record (declared use, omitted mechanism, consequence bound, explanatory dominance) in the body, where review attacks it like any content. There is no frontmatter mode field: undeclared text reads as universal. Mode is orthogonal to lifecycle stage — a note still at the conjecture stage may conjecture a universal or a tendency; declare both when both apply. Repair under review is mode-aware and runs in both directions: reframing a defeated universal down to statistical or ideal-type requires meeting the target mode's guard, and a claim hedged below its warrant is reframed up, not left vacuous.

## Title and body composability

**Claim titles by default.** Name the note like a claim, not a topic — something that could be true or false.

- *Composability test:* `since [title](./title.md)` or `because [title](./title.md)` reads naturally as prose.
- *Strength test:* the claim is contestable. "Continuous learning can happen outside of weights" passes; "continuous learning is substrate-independent" fails — nobody pushes back.

Add the `title-as-claim` trait when using one, so review gates check the promise.

**Body composability.** Another note should be able to cite this one as a premise without inheriting unrelated claims or examples. If a second cluster would poison imports, split it off or move it to `kb/work/`.

Exception: notes with the `synthesis` trait weave multiple cited claims into a single argument and are cited as a unit. Component claims that need to stand as citable premises should be extracted into their own notes.

Exceptions to claim titles: multi-claim specs, definitions, indexes, and exploratory drafts not ready to assert.

## Outbound links

Author each outbound link from the reader need at its source. A reciprocal link is allowed when the reverse direction independently helps readers; never add one merely to mirror an existing edge. Relationship symmetry describes semantics, not an authoring obligation: `contradicts` and `contrasts` are self-dual, while the other labels are directional. Find inbound links on demand with repository search; no backlink view is currently generated. Inline for strongest commitment, with a connective word that fits the argument (e.g. `since [title](path)`, `because [title](path)`, `but [title](path)`, `as in [title](path)`). Footer for labelled — `- [title](path) — label: context phrase`.

Scan `kb/theory/`, `kb/types/`, `kb/reference/`, `kb/agent-memory-systems/`, `kb/agentic-systems/`, `kb/sources/`, `kb/instructions/`, and `kb/tags/` for link targets. Do not link into `kb/work/` (workshop layer — value is consumed, not imported). Most links land within `kb/theory/` — the densest path. Outbound edges to `kb/instructions/` are rare — the usual direction is inverse (`instruction → note` via `rests-on`) — except `operationalized-from`, recorded as an `Operationalized into:` footer at this collection's methodology note when a procedure in `kb/instructions/` adds ordering, defaults, or stopping conditions the methodology doesn't itself fix; see the lineage semantics in `kb/reference/link-vocabulary.md`. Edges to `kb/sources/` point to the tracked ingest of the source the claim was abstracted from or that corroborates it, never to its local snapshot.

**Origin is not corroboration.** Evidence corroborates a claim only when it reports an attempt to refute that claim which the claim could have failed ([Popper, *Logic of Scientific Discovery*, §82 and appendix \*ix](../sources/popper-logic-of-scientific-discovery.ingest.md)). The rule is the same for internal evidence (session traces, reports, ADRs) and external sources; what decides is how the evidence was produced, not where it came from. A case or source the claim was built from is linked `abstracted-from`, never as corroboration of that claim. An `evidenced-by` link that claims corroboration says in its context phrase what the claim risked, and whether the evidence was recorded after the claim or independently of how it was built; otherwise the phrase says the evidence qualifies or bounds the claim. A corroboration appraisal is dated: it holds relative to the evidence accepted when it was made (§84).

**Labels:**

| label | kind | destinations | reader-need |
|---|---|---|---|
| `extends` | asym | theory | wants the argument developed further |
| `grounds` | asym | theory | wants to verify the premise |
| `enables` | asym | theory | wants the operational prerequisite |
| `exemplifies` | asym (instance→general) | theory | wants the general claim this instance falls under |
| `mechanism` | asym | theory | wants to understand how the claim operates |
| `contradicts` | sym | theory | wants to resolve a disagreement |
| `contrasts` | sym | theory | wants the neighbouring-shape distinction |
| `defined-in` | asym | theory/definitions, reference/definitions | reader may not know the term |
| `evidenced-by` | asym | theory, types, reference, reports/retained, agent-memory-systems, agentic-systems, sources, external | the target observation, case, or source corroborates, qualifies, or bounds this assertion; corroboration requires a test the claim could have failed (see "Origin is not corroboration") |
| `derived-from` | asym | reference, agent-memory-systems, agentic-systems, sources | claim is worked out from this source, adding nothing beyond it — see the lineage semantics in `kb/reference/link-vocabulary.md` |
| `abstracted-from` | asym | theory/evidence, reference, reports/retained, agent-memory-systems, agentic-systems, sources | claim generalizes beyond this source; the source is evidence, authority is earned by testing |
| `operationalized-from` | asym | instructions | procedure adds ordering, defaults, or stopping conditions this methodology note doesn't itself fix; not claim-preserving — see lineage semantics in `kb/reference/link-vocabulary.md` |
| `see-also` | asym | reference, agent-memory-systems, agentic-systems, sources, instructions | adjacent companion; use sparingly |

## Source grounding

A note's grounding check must fit one pass, so the note is bounded on the artifact side ([ADR 082](../reference/adr/082-grounding-is-bounded-on-the-artifact-by-unquoted-sources.md)): at most five distinct tracked sources (`kb/sources/*.ingest.md`) cited without a verbatim quotation paired to each. This contract sets the bound in its `unquoted-source-limit` field, so it holds for every artifact here, definitions and proposals included ([ADR 122](../reference/adr/122-collections-set-the-unquoted-source-limit.md)); `commonplace-validate` fails past five. A source is discharged by quoting it: a quoted span in the same paragraph as its link, marked `verbatim`, whose words occur in that ingest's `## Quotes` section — retain the quote through `cp-skill-ground`, never by editing the ingest. A source linked with `(snapshot required)` anywhere in the note always counts. Links to other notes never count; a linked note has passed its own grounding review, and this note owes it faithful representation, not re-grounding. Over the bound, quote or split by claim; a claim carried jointly by several sources is quoted together, not split.

Two conventions keep the bound honest:

- **A source cited as evidence is cited in the body.** A footer-only source citation has no sentence to carry its use, so nothing in the note can be checked against it and nothing can quote it. Either host it in a sentence or drop the entry.
- **A casebook hosts its retained evidence in prose.** When sources sit in table rows, put the quotes in a short block under the table — one sentence per source, naming the row — rather than in the cells.

## Definition placement

Definitions whose intended contribution supplies vocabulary for transferable
theory belong under `kb/theory/definitions/`. Definitions constituted by a
Commonplace selection, contract, or implemented classification belong under
`kb/reference/definitions/`. The `definition` type does not decide placement.

## Evidence placement

Use `kb/theory/evidence/` when a note's primary contribution is what a bounded dataset, experiment, trace cohort, or comparative casebook establishes about the design space. Apply the placement test to the inference: when, after Commonplace's choices are scoped, it concerns only those fixed choices or their measured effects (no free variable), the evidence note belongs in `kb/reports/retained/` beside the raw evidence, keeping the note type; a theory note may still cite it. These remain theoretical notes under this collection contract: state both the inference the evidence supports and its limit. The larger theory may still be incomplete, but the evidence artifact must make its own bounded inference. Keep observations whose theory-facing inference is unresolved in `kb/work/`; put first occurrences and pure pattern records without explanation in `kb/log.md`. Put raw captures in `kb/sources/` and descriptions retained to represent a particular system's current or historical state in that system's descriptive collection.

## Proposal placement

Use `kb/theory/proposals/` for finished theory the KB has not decided to import into its vocabulary: frameworks, distinctions, terms, and changes to adopted definitions. Placement follows adoption state, not doubt about the content; a conjecture that needs no new vocabulary is an ordinary note that states its conjectural force. Every artifact under `proposals/` carries the collection-local [`theory-proposal`](./types/theory-proposal.md) type, which states what a proposal must contain and how it is adopted or deleted ([ADR 084](../reference/adr/084-kind-rules-live-in-type-specs-and-operations-in-instructions.md)). Other notes may point to a proposal but do not cite it as a premise or use its terms as settled vocabulary.

## What does NOT belong here

- Unadopted system designs → `kb/reference/proposals/` (`design-proposal` type), unless recast as an existential claim per above
- Records of what Commonplace selected, and descriptions of the current or historical state those selections produced → `kb/reference/`
- Descriptions of a specific system's contract, interface, or current construction → `kb/reference/` for Commonplace, or `kb/agent-memory-systems/` and `kb/agentic-systems/` for external systems
- Procedures and how-to guidance → `kb/instructions/`
- Raw captures without frontmatter → `text` type, any collection
- Work in progress → `kb/work/` (workshops)

# Commission: Quote checking

## Intended contribution

Rebuild the existing artifact as a theory note about quote checking in general for readers designing or operating agent-operated knowledge bases. Explain what different checks establish, the assumptions that make their results meaningful, and what remains unverified. This is an explanatory topic treatment, not an operator procedure and not an effort to invent one overarching claim to justify a claim-shaped title. General reasoning must stand beyond Commonplace's selected implementation, which may supply bounded cases.

## Must keep

Keep the distinctions among wording agreement, attribution, contextual interpretation and truth of a quoted claim. Distinguish original and intermediary sources, retained material and material currently accessible to a checker, and mechanical matching from semantic judgment. Preserve the useful insight that a label alone cannot establish fidelity, but do not preserve the incumbent wording or taxonomy for its own sake. Explain mechanisms and limits rather than merely list these distinctions. A source larger than the available model context budget requires a selective or compressed representation in that context; this does not imply lossy storage in the larger system, nor loss of exactness in every selected passage. This constraint is subordinate to the note's purpose, not a required organizing argument.

## Must exclude

Do not conflate current model context, retained source evidence and the particular evidence a check actually used. Do not use 'ingest' as an unexplained universal stage that fixes fidelity permanently. Do not force second-hand provenance and verbatim wording into mutually exclusive categories. Do not infer semantic support, upstream authenticity or truth from string matching. Do not preserve the universal forced-lossy-retention claim, the mandatory locator-layer field or the same-offset argument merely because they occur in the incumbent. Do not reproduce a procedural checklist or turn this into documentation of Commonplace's current commands. No new named external-source claims are commissioned: the authorized basis is the listed repository artifacts and explicit reasoning. If external evidence is necessary, report the gap rather than invent support or browse uncommissioned sources.

## Reserved decisions

The user authorized a topic title, 'Quote checking', and explicitly approved an exception to this note's collection claim-title convention. Do not modify the collection contract. Keep type types/note.md; remove the title-as-claim trait. The workflow mechanically preserves the incumbent title/H1 and path: keep them temporarily for this candidate and report that the separately authorized retitle remains for the session agent after publication approval. Do not reshape the body to defend that temporary heading. Treat it as a known transition constraint when reviewing, not as a demand for the old claim.

Do not change dependents, source documents, tags/indexes or ADRs. Report specific dependent changes needed, including those needed to remove invalid implications. Publication of the candidate requires the user's separate approval. A lasting write brief is not yet authorized; propose its content after the candidate rather than silently adding one.

## Current direction

The user explicitly chose a theory note on quote checking in general, agreed to multistage writing, authorized reconsideration of the capture-time ceiling and layer taxonomy, and authorized this note's topic-title exception. The author may replace or drop the old 'fixed at capture/ingest' claim and 're-capture is the only remedy' formulation, and replace the three-layer taxonomy even though the role report says dependents rely on them. Preserve justified explanations, not known conflations. In the reconciliation report identify the impacts on ADR 046, the atomic-step note, the Peters–Chin-Yee and ROME ingests and the claims-and-grounding tag head, without editing them. Their use of the old note is compatibility information, not evidence that its claims are true. The role report is supplied separately by the workflow to the author/reviewer; reconstructors must not use the incumbent or its reviews as evidence.

The user found the first candidate too long and explicitly requested: 'rewrite it, compact it, remove the redundancies'. This revision must be substantially shorter, not a sentence-polish pass. Aim for about 650–850 words of body as an editorial target, not a reason to omit a necessary condition. Combine related distinctions into a few explanatory sections. State each limit once; do not repeatedly restate that string matching cannot establish meaning, attribution or truth. Keep the central mechanisms and useful distinctions from Must keep, but compress their presentation.

Lead with the explanation, not with a tour of ADRs. Cite ADRs at the claims or examples they support without repeatedly saying that they are merely one system's choices. Do not introduce an ADR then immediately discount its relevance. Remove drafting-process narration such as 'the following is this note's inference', 'no supplied source states it', 'the terms below are this note's definitions' and repeated source-scope disclaimers. Present explicit reasoning directly; put evidential accounting in the reconciliation report. Keep real uncertainty beside the affected claim, but do not substitute attribution disclaimers for reasoning. Avoid duplicative footer links and open questions that merely restate distinctions already explained. Drop peripheral branches rather than compressing every branch into a dense inventory. In particular, the full derived-copy argument, historical mismatch measurements, extraction heuristics and version-policy comparisons need not each have their own treatment; retain them only where they materially explain quote checking.

Exactness under normalization, source identity, occurrence/context selection and checks along a source chain are investigative avenues, not a mandatory section outline. The source-first workers choose a compact supported argument. Do not repeat the prior candidate's unsupported phrase 'does not suppress recomputation'. Do not imply that unresolved-case reporting detects quotations an extractor misses entirely, that a version pin by itself detects every later edit, or that locating a unique occurrence proves authorial intent. Preserve the distinction between a check's tested property and conclusions it cannot establish.

# Account for the claims of a rewrite

Goal: the claim selection of the rewrite is fixed from the evidence before
anyone sees the existing note, so that the note cannot lend warrant to its
own claims.

Consumption: the rewrite workflow (`commonplace-review run rewrite`) gives
this file to a fresh headless worker as its `instruction` input. The prompt
names the other inputs and the output file. Nothing else is inherited.

The workflow freezes your claim account. A later fresh worker writes the
candidate from it. So the account carries the judgment of what the note
claims; write it so that another writer can follow it.

## Inputs

- `commission`: the operator's current direction for this rewrite and the
  sources with their roles. When the note has no write brief, it also states
  the intended contribution and reader update, what to keep and exclude, and
  the decisions reserved for the operator. When the note has a brief, it
  holds only what this rewrite adds to the brief, and it names any brief item
  the operator amended for this rewrite.
- `brief`, when present: the note's write brief. It is binding retained
  intent. Its Intent, Must keep, Must exclude and Reserved decisions hold
  together with the commission's additions. A commission that only adds to
  the brief does not contradict it.
- `reconstruction`: the source-faithful basis. It separates support from
  inference and names conflicts, scope and gaps.
- `type-contract` and `collection-contract`, when present: the contracts the
  note must meet.

## What you must not do

- Do not read the note, its write brief file, its earlier texts in git
  history or under `kb/reports/`, or any file that quotes it.
- Read no repository file. The inputs are the whole evidence for this step.
- Do not add a commitment the reconstruction does not support or infer.
- Do not make a decision the commission reserves for the operator. Name it
  as reserved instead.
- Do not write the note's prose. Write nothing except the output file.

## Procedure

1. If the commission and the brief contradict each other, write the problem
   file and name both passages.
2. List the material commitments of the reconstruction: each claim,
   definition or distinction the contribution could rest on.
3. For each, decide its treatment: state it, state it with a qualifier,
   state it as inference, leave it out, or leave it to the operator. Give
   the basis in the reconstruction, the scope and qualifiers it needs, what
   it depends on, and where it goes in the note.
4. Say what the note must not claim because the reconstruction names it as a
   gap or a conflict.

## Output

Write the claim account as Markdown with one `## ` section per material
commitment. Code checks that there is at least one such section. Each
section names the commitment, its treatment, its basis, its scope and
qualifiers, its dependencies and its destination in the note. You may end
with a section of commitments the note must not make.

# Reconstruction: Quote checking

Basis for a compact theory note on quote checking in general: what different
checks establish, the assumptions that make their results meaningful, and what
remains unverified. No write brief was supplied; the commission alone states
intent. The commission and the inputs do not contradict each other.

Source keys used below:

- S1 = `kb/reference/adr/046-verbatim-quotes-are-validated-against-their-cited-source.md` (input `source-1`)
- S2 = `kb/reference/adr/073-untracked-source-snapshots-require-ingest-grounding.md` (input `source-2`)
- S3 = `kb/reference/adr/094-quotations-require-a-unique-occurrence-or-a-containing-range.md` (input `source-3`)
- S4 = `kb/theory/a-derived-copy-of-recomputable-truth-must-be-checked-or-absent.md` (input `source-4`)

Line locators refer to the captured inputs.

S1, S2 and S3 are Commonplace decision records. They support claims about what
one checking design selected and why, plus the general reasons they give for
those selections. S4 is a theory note whose strongest claims are themselves
under assessment. S1 line 39 links to the note being rewritten. That link is
compatibility information, not evidence; nothing below relies on it.

## Support

### 1. A quote marker is an assertion. Unchecked, it is trusted on the author's word

- S1 Context, ln 17: "A `verbatim` citation asserts that a quoted span is copied exactly from a source retained in the KB." Before the decision, "nothing checked it: an author wrote a quote, wrote `verbatim`, and the claim was hand-maintained and trusted."
- S1 Consequences, ln 39: once checked, the `verbatim` marker "becomes load-bearing rather than decorative"; it is "the only one that can be mechanically falsified." `paraphrase layer` and `second-hand` "remain unchecked by construction — they never claimed exact text, and no derivation rule exists for them."
- S4 Consequences, ln 40: "Never write the unenforced natural-language version of a checkable claim … A checkable claim is enforced as a check or not asserted at all." (This is S4's strongest form; see Inference 6 for its applicability.)

### 2. A string check tests wording agreement only

- S3 Context, ln 21–23: "The evidence boundary must remain separate from mechanical matching. Finding one occurrence cannot establish that its context supports the attached claim."
- S3 Consequences, ln 121–123: "The checker establishes occurrence, uniqueness, and range containment under its normalization rule. It does not establish truth, relevance, or semantic support."
- S2 Considered alternatives, ln 128–131: storing a verbatim copy of every note claim would make exact matching possible, "but … string equality would still not establish source support."
- S4 precondition 1, ln 32: a derivation rule exists for "extractable lists, set memberships, and file identity"; "natural-language summaries and judgments do not — there is no comparison a machine can run."

### 3. Exactness is relative to a normalization rule, and the rule matters in both directions

- S1 ln 21: a prototype run found 63 match, 18 mismatch, 6 unresolved across 87 candidates, "with no false mismatch on manual audit." Mismatches were "real failures of the strict assertion, dominated by editorial omission (`...`), bracketed substitution, case changes, and punctuation moved inside the quotation boundary." Scope: one sibling casebook corpus.
- S1 ln 43: normalization ("quote-mark folding, whitespace collapse, emphasis stripping, `NFKC`") "is load-bearing, not polish: an under-normalized checker would produce false mismatches on correct quotes, which is worse than no check."
- S3 Decision, ln 52–59: normalization differs by source kind. Git blobs, analysis captures and repository snapshots use whitespace-only normalization; ordinary KB Markdown and web or paper snapshots also normalize typography and Markdown emphasis. "The source resolver selects the rule, never a per-citation switch."
- S3 ln 47: "Slice original source lines before normalization."

### 4. Occurrence is not location: presence, uniqueness and containment are different tests

- S3 Context, ln 15–18: "A quotation can occur in a source without identifying one occurrence. A plausible line range can point elsewhere in the same file. Presence and range bounds alone do not establish that the cited passage occupies the location an author gives it."
- S3 Decision, ln 45–50: require exactly one occurrence in the eligible region; with a range, exactly one complete occurrence inside it. "Separate extracts and disjoint ranges remain separate regions; they cannot form a synthetic passage by concatenation." A repeated quote without a range fails with its occurrence count; two occurrences on one line require more quoted context.
- S3 Decision, ln 62–64: a path "may carry a checked line range; a trailing locator note supplies context but is not evidence."
- S2 Consequences, ln 166–168: "source locations remain authored locators rather than mechanically verified anchors" (pre-ADR-094 state, amended per S2 ln 15).
- S1 Decision, ln 25 (historical): pairing is by proximity to "the markdown source it links"; S1 ln 19 called the derivation rule "a strict substring test".

### 5. Which source? Identity of the compared bytes

- S2 Context, ln 19–23: snapshots are "ignored local reading copies. A fresh checkout therefore retains an ingest's source identity and snapshot checksum, but not the complete captured source." Ingest analysis is tracked, but its summaries and judgments "are interpretations. They are not source text."
- S2 Decision, ln 68–73 (snapshot route): the checker derives one exact path, "verifies exact-byte SHA-256 and canonical source equality against the ingest", and treats missing, mismatched or unreadable bytes as failure, "not a warning or an invitation to find another copy."
- S2 Considered alternatives, ln 154–156: "Equal bytes do not bind a local path to the ingest being cited. Exact name pairing makes the declared dependency inspectable; the checksum then verifies the bytes at that path."
- S2 ln 99–104: a snapshot checksum is immutable; "changed source bytes are a new observation and require a distinct snapshot basename and ingest path."
- S3 Decision, ln 68–73: KB prose citations "remain unversioned and are checked against current bytes"; an append does not invalidate every citation; "a removed or changed supporting passage can still fail its next check." "Missing source bytes are reported separately from an absent quotation and never count as verified."
- S3 Considered alternatives, ln 100–103: hash-pinning every living target "detects all target edits but cannot distinguish relevant changes from unrelated appends." Current-byte verification "does not detect a changed interpretive context when the quoted words remain unchanged."

### 6. Retained material, accessible material, and the material a check actually used

- S2 Context, ln 30–34: "A bounded verbatim passage may contain enough source material to judge the note's use. Some claims instead depend on broad, distributed, or contextual material that cannot be represented soundly by a small set of retained quotes. The full snapshot is then required, but it cannot be assumed to exist on every machine."
- S2 Decision, ln 62–67 (quotes route): reviewers read only the retained verbatim extracts as support and ignore analytical sections; "If the quotes are insufficient, the check fails; it never silently falls back to a local snapshot."
- S2 Considered alternatives, ln 142–145: automatic fallback "would make the same note pass or fail according to ambient cache state without declaring that dependency."
- S3 Decision, ln 64–66: notes citing an ingest search only its Quotes blockquote bodies; "Verification against those bodies does not imply that the separate snapshot check ran on this machine."
- S3 ln 72–73 and ln 118–119: unavailable ingest snapshots "remain explicitly unverified".
- S2 ln 50–54: retained passages are appended only after the exact snapshot's canonical source and checksum are verified, and each passage is checked to occur in those bytes.

### 7. Intermediaries and semantic hops

- S2 Context, ln 25–28: checking a note against an ingest paraphrase "that was itself checked against the source creates two semantic hops, and rewording at either hop can change the proposition; the ledger makes the judgment easier to run but not sound."
- S2 Consequences, ln 160–163: "The semantic check is direct: note claim to source quote, or note claim to the full pinned source. Ingest analysis … cannot acquire source authority by being tracked."
- S2 ln 116–118 (corpus measurement): only 4 of 65 sampled note-to-ingest pairs reused the normalized claim string. Scope: one Commonplace corpus.
- S2 ln 77–79: target-specific transfer reasoning stays in the citing artifact and is checked as an inference, "rather than asking the source to contain the target's conclusion."

### 8. Semantic judgment is a separate check with a different cost

- S2 Decision, ln 58–60: source-dependent claims are checked directly against source material with a semantic grounding-alignment test.
- S4 ln 20: where verification is judgment, it is "a Level B check … an LLM reading both and judging fidelity or support — too costly to run always and too noisy to block on."
- S4 ln 22: mechanical derivation makes verification "Level A — deterministic, near-zero cost, binary, runnable on every pass."

### 9. What the checker does not see

- S1 Decision, ln 30 and Consequences, ln 43: "The extraction heuristic is not complete, and `unresolved` is how it says so rather than passing silently." Unresolved means "an unpaired verbatim citation" — a marked candidate the parser found but could not pair with a source. S1 warns on it only in notes with at least one resolvable verbatim quote, to avoid firing in text that merely writes about the convention.
- S1 Decision, ln 35 and S3 Consequences, ln 110–112: quotations shown inside code blocks or recognized quotation bodies are demonstrations, not assertions; checkers exclude them so "source examples are not treated as author assertions."

### 10. Severity follows the asymmetry between a false and an absent claim

- S1 Decision, ln 29: "mismatch → fail. The note asserts a falsehood. Per the derived-copy rule the false-copy failure mode is silent and unbounded, so it cannot be a warning."
- S4 ln 14–16: an absent copy costs "one bounded recomputation"; a false copy "can cause silent, unbounded wrongness when it tells consumers to stop looking".
- S4 ln 30–35: enforcement requires (1) a derivation rule, (2) a machine-locatable region naming its source, (3) ground truth that exists at validation time, (4) a validator that is a strict mechanical extraction, centralized and amortized.
- S1 Context, ln 19: claimed all four preconditions held for its quote check, including "the source snapshot is a checked-in file present at validation time."

## Inference

I1. **A check verifies one relation between two specified texts under a rule.**
A quote check takes a quoted span, a resolved source and a normalization rule.
It returns whether the span occurs (once, inside a range) in that source.
Rests on Support 2, 3, 4. Consequences: (a) the result has no meaning without
saying which bytes were compared (Support 5, 6); (b) "exact" means "equal after
this normalization", so a policy choice, not the text alone, fixes what counts
as agreement (Support 3).

I2. **Four questions are separable, and a string check answers only the first.**
(i) Wording agreement: do these words occur in the compared text? (ii)
Attribution: is the compared text the source the citation names, and did the
named author produce it? (iii) Context: does the passage, read where it occurs,
support the use the citing text makes of it? (iv) Truth: is the quoted claim
true? Support 2 rules out (iii) and (iv) from occurrence. Support 5 shows that
identity checks (checksum, canonical-source equality, name pairing) address
part of (ii): they bind the compared bytes to a recorded capture. Nothing in the
sources checks that the capture faithfully represents the original or that the
attributed author wrote it. That upstream part of (ii) is therefore unverified
by any mechanism in the sources (see Gaps).

I3. **Normalization is a two-sided error budget.** Too little normalization
fails correct quotes (S1 ln 43); too much could let substantive edits pass
(inferred: the editorial omissions and bracketed substitutions S1 ln 21 counts
as real mismatches would pass a rule that ignored them). Per-source-kind rules
(S3 ln 52–59) follow from the fact that typography and emphasis are noise in
prose snapshots but can be content in code. Rests on Support 3. S3 states the
rule split but does not state this reason explicitly; the code-content reason is
inference.

I4. **Uniqueness and containment address location, not intent.** A unique
occurrence, or one occurrence inside a checked range, removes ambiguity about
*which* passage the quote is equal to (Support 4). It does not show that the
author meant that passage or that the passage supports the use (Support 2,
S3 ln 21–23). Forbidding concatenation of disjoint ranges (S3 ln 47–49) blocks a
check from certifying a passage that never existed contiguously in the source.

I5. **A pass is relative to the evidence the check actually had.** The same
citation can be checked against (a) an original source, (b) a retained
capture of it, (c) an intermediary's retained extract, or (d) nothing, if bytes
are missing. Support 6 shows a design that keeps these apart: checking against
retained extracts does not imply the capture was checked on this machine; missing
bytes never count as verified; no silent fallback to whatever copy is present.
Generalization: a check result should be read as "agrees with the evidence used",
and retained-but-unavailable material or material merely present in a model's
context is not the evidence a given check used. Rests on S2 ln 30–34, 62–67,
142–145; S3 ln 64–66, 72–73.

I6. **Exactness and second-hand provenance are independent axes.** A quote of
an intermediary's retained extract can be exact with respect to that extract
(S3 ln 64–66) while being second-hand with respect to the original. S2's
retention step checks extracts against the capture at append time (S2 ln 50–54),
so a chain of exact checks is possible; each link verifies only its own pair.
S1's marker set (ln 17) treats `verbatim` and `second-hand` as alternative
markers on one citation; the inference here is that this is a labelling choice,
not a property of quotation. Rests on Support 1, 6, 7.

I7. **Semantic hops compound; string hops can chain.** Paraphrase-to-paraphrase
checking adds a judgment at each hop (S2 ln 25–28). Exact extracts verified
against pinned bytes let a later semantic check go directly to source wording
(S2 ln 160–163). Inference: retaining exact source material moves the single
necessary judgment to one place; it does not remove it. Rests on Support 7, 8.

I8. **The derived-copy argument applies to the wording relation only, and only
when its preconditions hold.** The quoted span is a copy of a source span, and
occurrence is mechanically recomputable (S4 precondition 1). Two limits:
(a) the *choice* of span and its claimed use are not recomputable, so S4's
enforce-or-omit rule covers wording agreement, not support (Support 2, S4 ln
32); (b) precondition 3 (ground truth present at validation time) fails where
captures are untracked local copies (S2 ln 19–23); S1 ln 19 asserted it held
for its corpus. Where it fails, a design must either retain enough exact
material (quotes route) or declare the dependency and fail closed (snapshot
route) — S2's two routes. Whether S4's "forbidden" (rather than "risky") verdict
transfers depends on S4's asymmetry argument (ln 14–16), which the sources do
not test for quotations specifically.

I9. **A version pin records identity; detection needs a comparison.** S3 ln
100–103 says hash-pinning living targets "detects all target edits"; that
detection occurs only when a later check compares current bytes to the pin.
A frozen capture (S2 ln 99–104, S3 ln 70–71) is stable by construction and
therefore cannot show later changes to the upstream original. Current-byte
checking catches changed or removed passages at the next check but misses a
changed surrounding context when the quoted words survive (S3 ln 102–103).
Rests on Support 5.

I10. **`unresolved` reports pairing failures among recognized candidates.** A
quotation the extractor never recognized as a verbatim-marked candidate does
not appear in any outcome. Rests on S1 ln 30, 43 (defines unresolved as an
unpaired verbatim citation). The sources give no measure of such misses.

I11. **Context budget (reasoning only, no source support).** A source larger
than a checker's or reader's available context must be represented there by
selected passages or a compressed form. S2 ln 30–34 is the nearest supported
point: some claims depend on broad or distributed material that a small set of
retained quotes cannot soundly represent, so the full capture is required. The
inference that selection in context implies neither lossy storage in the larger
system nor loss of exactness in each selected passage follows from Support 6
(full captures retained with checksums; extracts checked exactly) but no source
discusses model context budgets.

## Conflicts

C1. **Substring presence vs. unique occurrence.** S1 ln 19 treats the derivation
rule as "a strict substring test" and ln 25 pairs by proximity. S3 ln 15–18 and
45–50 hold that presence alone does not establish the cited passage and require
uniqueness or range containment. S3 is the later, amending decision; it settles
the policy for that system. As general theory the sources disagree on whether
presence suffices as the tested property; S3 gives the reason (repeated
occurrences, misleading ranges).

C2. **Ground truth present at validation time.** S1 ln 19 says the source
snapshot "is a checked-in file present at validation time." S2 ln 19–23 says
primary-source snapshots are ignored local copies absent from a fresh checkout.
These may concern different source kinds (S1's prototype ran over a casebook
corpus linking Markdown sources), but S1 states its precondition generally. Not
settled by the sources beyond S2 being later and S3 ln 72–73 treating ingest
snapshot absence as "conditional and non-blocking".

C3. **Normalization scope.** S1 ln 43 lists one normalization set as load-bearing
(quote folding, whitespace, emphasis, NFKC). S3 ln 52–59 restricts some source
kinds to whitespace-only. S3 is later and settles the selected policy; S1's
general claim that under-normalization is worse than no check and S3's
narrowing for code-like sources pull in different directions for a general
theory.

C4. **Hash pins: "detects all edits" vs. insufficiency.** S3 ln 100–101 says
hash-pinning "detects all target edits". The commission forbids implying that a
version pin by itself detects every later edit. Not a conflict between sources;
I9 reconciles by locating detection in the later comparison. Flagged so the
author does not import S3's wording unqualified.

C5. **Hand-maintained claims: forbidden vs. unavoidable (internal to S4).** S4
ln 10 and 16 forbid hand-maintained-and-trusted copies; S4 ln 20 says in the
judgment regime the hand-maintained dependent artifact "is not forbidden; it is
unavoidable". S4 resolves this by regime (check price). For quote checking this
splits wording (Level A) from support (Level B); see I8.

## Scope

- S1–S3 describe one system's quotation-checking design over Markdown KB
  sources, Git blobs, analysis captures and web/paper/repository snapshots. Their
  general reasons (Support 2, 4, 5, 6, 7) stand without the specific commands,
  marker syntax or file layouts; their policies (thresholds such as "two to ten
  occurrences", per-kind normalization sets, append-only Quotes, severity
  levels) are selections.
- S1's numbers (87 candidates; 63/18/6) and S2's (4 of 65; 119 paraphrased vs
  374 extracts) come from single Commonplace corpora; they illustrate
  mismatch kinds and paraphrase drift but do not estimate rates elsewhere.
- S1 is historical and amended (by S3; terminology note ln 13). S2's ingest
  syntax is amended by S3 (S2 ln 15); its route distinction remains.
- S3's constructor clauses are amended by ADR 105 (S3 ln 11); S3 says
  normalization and uniqueness remain current. ADR 105 is not an authorized
  source.
- S4's preconditions and asymmetry are stated for derived copies of
  recomputable truth generally; their application to quotations is the
  inference in I8, not something S4 tests.
- All support concerns textual sources with retrievable bytes. Nothing covers
  audio, images, oral quotation, or sources whose original is no longer
  retrievable.

## Gaps

- **Upstream authenticity and authorship attribution.** No source gives a
  mechanism or argument for checking that a capture faithfully represents the
  original publication or that the attributed author produced the words. Only
  binding of compared bytes to a recorded capture is supported (Support 5).
- **Model context budget.** No source discusses context limits, selective or
  compressed in-context representation, or its relation to storage. Commission
  requires the point; it must rest on explicit reasoning (I11).
- **Legitimate editorial alteration.** S1 counts ellipsis, brackets and case
  changes as mismatches of the strict assertion; S3 forbids concatenating
  disjoint ranges. No source discusses a contract under which marked editorial
  alterations could be checked as such (e.g. segment-wise), or whether quoting
  conventions that permit them should be supported.
- **Extractor miss rate.** No measurement of quotations the extractor never
  recognizes (I10).
- **Reliability of semantic checks.** S4 calls Level B checks costly and noisy;
  no source measures how well semantic grounding judgments detect
  out-of-context use.
- **Context drift with unchanged words.** S3 ln 102–103 names the blind spot;
  no source proposes or evaluates a detector.
- **Definitions.** "Fidelity", "attribution", "contextual interpretation",
  "intermediary source" and "capture" have no definitions in the sources. "Ingest"
  and "snapshot" are defined only as Commonplace artifacts (S2 ln 19–23,
  36–39); the commission forbids using "ingest" as an unexplained universal
  stage.
- **External evidence.** No external (non-repository) evidence on quotation
  practice in scholarship, journalism or other KB systems is authorized. Any
  claim that the distinctions transfer beyond agent-operated KBs rests on
  reasoning alone.
inputs.type-contract.md:
---
type: types/type-spec.md
name: note
description: Base structured document type for transferable KB notes with optional committed human verification
schema: ./note.schema.yaml
---

# Note

Use `note` for transferable KB claims, observations, and theory that are worth preserving beyond the current task. A note is a structured markdown artifact with YAML frontmatter, a prose title, and enough body context for an agent to decide how to use it.

## Frontmatter

| Field | Required | Use |
|---|---:|---|
| `type` | Yes | `types/note.md` |
| `description` | Yes | Discriminating retrieval filter, not a summary. |
| `traits` | No | Independently checkable review expectations. |
| `tags` | No | Navigation tags used by indexes. |
| `user-verified` | No | May only be `true`; records explicit human attestation to the current substantive contents. |

## Description

The description should answer "why this document?" for a future retrieval decision. It should distinguish the note from nearby notes and usually fit in one sentence.

## User verification

`user-verified: true` means a human user explicitly attests that the artifact's current substantive contents have been verified. Absence means only that there is no current user attestation; it says nothing about truth, maturity, currency, or review history.

Creation, conversion, deterministic validation, and semantic review do not confer human verification; their outputs must not carry a newly granted `user-verified` field. After a substantive edit, the field must be absent until a human explicitly verifies the revised contents. An existing attestation remains valid across a mechanical change only when that change is covered by an explicit human-approved trivial-change workflow.

## Traits

Traits route semantic review. They do not change structural validation.

| Trait | What it asserts |
|---|---|
| `title-as-claim` | The title is a proposition that can be true or false. |
| `definition` | The note pins a term's operational meaning. |
| `has-comparison` | The note compares alternatives. |
| `has-external-sources` | The note cites material outside the project. |
| `has-implementation` | The note includes implementation sketches or code-facing detail. |
| `synthesis` | The note composes multiple cited claims into a unified argument; cite as a unit and expect inline restatement. Waives the default body-composability rule. |

## Writing Shape

- Use the title as the strongest compressed handle for the note.
- Put the main claim or mechanism near the top.
- Link to adjacent notes where the relationship helps traversal.
- Keep design rationale in notes; keep imperative procedure in instructions.
- State the claim's limits under their own heading (`## Scope`): assumptions, applicability conditions, known failure cases. A limit with its own section can be narrowed by a rescoping edit without rewriting the claim, and the review gates that test scope look for it. Omit the section when no limit is known. `structured-claim` notes use `## Caveats` for the same role.

## Template

```markdown
---
description: ""
type: types/note.md
traits: []
tags: []
---

# {prose-as-title — a proposition, not a topic label}

{Your analysis, reasoning, or exploration. Freeform.}

## Scope

- {Assumptions, applicability conditions, known failure cases — omit section if none}

## Open Questions

- {Unresolved points worth tracking — omit section if none}

---

Relevant Notes:

- [related-note](./related-note.md) — how it relates
```

---

Relevant Notes:

- [text](./text.md) - implicit no-frontmatter capture state that can be promoted to a note
- [document-types-should-be-verifiable](../theory/document-types-should-be-verifiable.md) - design rationale for verifiable types
